initial_requirements: Developers building multi-agent systems need an expanded agentMom framework that provides reusable communication capabilities for agents and their conversations. Agents should be able to communicate with one recipient, selected groups, or all agents on a local network, join and leave communication groups, and choose whether messages require protection. The new framework must remain usable with applications based on the existing agentMom environment.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Hello, I'm GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. I’ll be gathering detailed information about the agentMom Multi-Agent Communication Framework so we can clearly understand what needs to be built and how it should work. Before we begin, are you aligned with this interview scope, or do you expect something different?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, that scope sounds right to me. We’re looking at extending agentMom so agents can communicate more flexibly, including targeted, group, and broadcast messaging, while still fitting into the existing environment. I’m aligned with that and ready to discuss the details.

turns.interviewer_utterance: To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I’m speaking as the stakeholder representing the needs of the teams that build and run multi-agent applications on top of agentMom. My connection is that I’m responsible for making sure the framework supports practical agent communication without breaking existing applications.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Thank you. Could you describe the current agent communication process or system you use in agentMom today?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Right now, communication is pretty limited and mostly tied to the existing agentMom setup rather than being a reusable framework feature. In practice, agents can exchange messages in a more application-specific way, but we don’t have a standardized, flexible communication layer for one-to-one, group, or network-wide messaging. That’s why we want this expansion.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What current communication processes do you want to change or improve, or what features do you hope to get from this project?
turns.interviewee_utterance: We want to make messaging much more reusable and structured, so developers don’t have to build communication logic into each application from scratch. The main improvement is supporting direct messages, group conversations, and broadcasts across agents on the local network, plus the ability for agents to join or leave groups dynamically. We also want a clear way to mark messages as protected when needed.

turns.interviewer_utterance: So the main features you want are direct messaging, group conversations, broadcast messaging on the local network, dynamic group join/leave, and the option to protect messages, right?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, that’s correct. Those are the core capabilities we need in the new framework, along with keeping it compatible with applications already using agentMom.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Are there any other features you would like to see in this project, perhaps something that has not been the primary focus so far?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Nothing major beyond those core communication capabilities, at least not as an initial requirement. Compatibility with the existing agentMom environment is the main extra concern, because we don’t want to force people to rewrite current applications. If there are other features, I’d want to verify them with the development team before committing to them.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Based on your description, do you think message delivery acknowledgement or status feedback should also be included?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, I think some form of acknowledgment or delivery status would be very useful, especially for direct messages and protected messages. It doesn’t have to be overly complex, but developers should be able to tell whether a message was accepted or delivered successfully. I’d want to confirm how far that needs to go, though, because we may not need full reliability tracking for every broadcast.

turns.interviewer_utterance: You mentioned acknowledgments and delivery status for direct and protected messages, with possibly lighter handling for broadcasts. Could you describe what you want those acknowledgments to accomplish?
turns.interviewee_utterance: They should mainly confirm that a message reached the intended recipient and was processed at least at a basic transport level. For protected messages, I’d also want confidence that the message was handled securely, not just sent. For broadcasts, a simple “sent” or “accepted” response is probably enough since waiting for every agent to respond would be too heavy.
